name: Question 15
problem:
Given that for $s>\omega ,$

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\omega t)}=\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}-{\omega }^{2}},\,L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\omega t)}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}-{\omega }^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

find the Laplace transform of $f(t)=2\operatorname{cosh}⁡(9t)+6\operatorname{sinh}⁡(9t)$ for $s>9.$
worked_solution:
The linearity property of the Laplace transform states that for functions $f(t)$ and $g(t),$ we have

$$
L{\alpha f(t)+\beta g(t)}=\alpha \cdot L{f(t)}+\beta \cdot L{g(t)},
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants.

Taking the Laplace transform and applying the linearity property, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{2\operatorname{cosh}⁡(9t)+6\operatorname{sinh}⁡(9t)} & =L{2\operatorname{cosh}⁡(9t)}+L{6\operatorname{sinh}⁡(9t)} \\  & =2L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(9t)}+6L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(9t)}.\end{aligned}
$$

We are given that

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\omega t)} & =\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}-{\omega }^{2}}, &  & s>\omega , \\ L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\omega t)} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}-{\omega }^{2}}, &  & s>\omega .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(9t)} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}-81},\,s>9 \\ L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(9t)} & =\frac{9}{{s}^{2}-81},\,s>9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Laplace transform of $f(t)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =2L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(9t)}+6L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(9t)} \\  & =2\cdot \frac{s}{{s}^{2}-81}+6\cdot \frac{9}{{s}^{2}-81} \\  & =\frac{2s}{{s}^{2}-81}+\frac{54}{{s}^{2}-81} \\  & =\frac{2s+54}{{s}^{2}-81}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Given that for s>ω, L{sinh⁡(ωt)}=ωs2−ω2,L{cosh⁡(ωt)}=ss2−ω2, find the Laplace transform of f(t)=2cosh⁡(9t)+6sinh⁡(9t) for s>9.

a
18s−54s2−81
b
6s−18s2−81
c
2s+549(s2−81)
d
2s+54s2−81
e
s+54s2−81
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The linearity property of the Laplace transform states that for functions f(t) and g(t), we have L{αf(t)+βg(t)}=α⋅L{f(t)}+β⋅L{g(t)}, where α and β are constants.

Taking the Laplace transform and applying the linearity property, we have L{2cosh⁡(9t)+6sinh⁡(9t)}=L{2cosh⁡(9t)}+L{6sinh⁡(9t)}=2L{cosh⁡(9t)}+6L{sinh⁡(9t)}.

We are given that L{sinh⁡(ωt)}=ωs2−ω2,s>ω,L{cosh⁡(ωt)}=ss2−ω2,s>ω.

Therefore, we have the following: L{cosh⁡(9t)}=ss2−81,s>9L{sinh⁡(9t)}=9s2−81,s>9

Therefore, the Laplace transform of f(t) is L{f(t)}=2L{cosh⁡(9t)}+6L{sinh⁡(9t)}=2⋅ss2−81+6⋅9s2−81=2ss2−81+54s2−81=2s+54s2−81.
